Top-tier growth stock at a steep discount
Quarterly OP exceeds W100tr despite FX headwinds
We maintain our target price of W400,000 for Samsung Electronics (SEC). The stock remains undervalued in absolute terms, trading at a 2027F P/E of 3.2x and P/B of 1.2x. Notably, our target price implies multiples of just 5.4x and 2.5x, respectively. We forecast operating profit at W139tr (+29% QoQ) for 4Q26 and W622tr (+58% YoY) for 2027.
For 3Q26, the company reported revenue of W195.3tr (+14% QoQ) and operating profit of W107.4tr (+20% QoQ). Excluding roughly W10tr in adverse FX effects, operating profit would have reached around W120tr. Higher memory prices drove intersegment sales to a record W16tr (+115% YoY), but the resulting increase in component costs contributed to an 8.8%p YoY decline in the DX division’s OP margin.
In 3Q26, DRAM and NAND bit shipments increased 3% and 5% QoQ, respectively, while ASPs rose 19% and 18%, respectively. HBM4 revenue more than tripled QoQ, lifting its share of total HBM revenue to around 60%. For 4Q26, we forecast DRAM bit shipment growth of 17% and ASP growth of 10%, alongside NAND bit shipment growth of 15% and ASP growth of 10%. OP margins should remain elevated at 82% for DRAM and 67% for NAND.
Memory visibility through 2030; foundry recovery from 2027
We expect capex in the DS division to make only a limited contribution to bit shipment growth in 2028, given the time required from fab construction to wafer production and longer equipment delivery lead times. Larger dies and additional metal layers for HBM4E and HBM5 should also increase the amount of conventional DRAM output displaced by HBM production. Against this backdrop, SEC expects industry-wide DRAM supply conditions to remain tight through 2028.
For 2027, we forecast DRAM bit shipment growth of 22% and ASP growth of 33%, alongside NAND bit shipment growth of 22% and ASP growth of 26%. OP margins are likely to hold steady YoY at 80% for DRAM and 67% for NAND. SEC has signed long-term supply agreements with 10 major customers and is in negotiations with another 10. Its target of having 60?70% of capacity through 2030 covered by long-term agreements is looking increasingly achievable.
We estimate that foundry business earnings approached break-even levels excluding provisions for performance bonuses. The number of 2nm projects secured in 2026 is expected to more than double YoY, led by major cloud service providers and AI/high-performance computing (HPC) customers. In 2027, HPC should account for over 50% of foundry revenue, while utilization at 8nm and below is expected to exceed 100%. Synergies from HBM4 base dies should further accelerate earnings improvement.
